map.hc9_main:0.event.0.description:
I traveled here and there for a while...  

Antagarich is full of opportunities for a powerful Lich like me.  At long last, my travels led me to this new continent, Erathia.  

It seems that my timing is perfect.  A mindless Barbarian named Tarnum brought the powerful Empire of Bracaduun to its knees and was later on crushed by the upstart kingdom of Erathia.  

Erathia's new King, Rion Gryphonheart, eventually faced Tarnum in battle and killed him.  All these struggles have weakened the locals.  Time to introduce some further chaos and anguish in this land.
map.hc9_main:0.event.1.description:
I like this Tarnum fellow.  He is said to be as ruthless and cruel as I am; even though he wasn't undead to begin with.  

It seems that this land has never even witnessed the undead lurking about.  The undead were only part of children's stories in this part of the World.  It's time to change that.  I will lay low for the moment of course.  I need to gather up my strength before I will be able to unleash my full power.

I built up a small base of opperation in a hidden valley.  It is virtually unreacheable but will grand me a small income to cover my expenses.
map.hc9_main:0.event.2.description: As fortune would have it, I was able to save my powerful cloak.  The ignorant knights deemed it only symbolic but in truth it is enchanted with powerful magic.  With it, I am able to raise Liches from the bodies of my fallen enemies.  My army grows stronger by the minute.
map.hc9_main:0.event.3.description:
It seems that even in death, this so called Barbarian King Tarnum, still holds sway over the hearts of men.  Tales of his cruelty still circulate the towns' taverns and (since my arrival) the witnessing of undead corpses lurking around has empowered those tales. 

The townsfolk begin to quiver to the thought of the cruel Barbarian King ever be risen from the dead and seek vengeance upon the land. 

Actually, this is no bad idea.  Why not reanimate Tarnum's corpse and keep him as one of my minions?   Even in death he remains as fearsome as ever and he will surely prove useful to my ascent towards a new throne.
map.hc9_main:0.event.4.description:
Tarnum's body is buried somewhere in this region.  It is guarded by a horde of Barbarian Chieftains that still rule this land.  It seems that the Erathian King didn't crush the Barbarians entirely but allowed them to live in this part of Erathia called Krewlod.  They are weakened by the long years of oppression of course but may still pose as a threat.

My escapades haven't passed unnoticed.  The rumors of an undead army spread like wildfire and now the Erathians know that the afterlife isn't just a fairy tale.  I must tread lightly and focus on reaching Tarnum's tomb in time.
map.hc9_main:0.event.5.description:
I am close now.  I must hurry and reach Tarnum's tomb in time, before his corpse has decayed in such a degree that it would be impossible to reanimate it.

The barbarian Chieftains have rallied their forces and block the path that leads to the underground passage where Tarnum was buried.  It seems that I drew their attention at last and they will gather their full strength before they attack.  

It matters not.  Soon they will have to face Tarnum's prowess as well.  Between the two of us there can be no victory!
map.hc9_main:0.event.6.description:
Treachery...  and then Deceit.

It was easy for me to poison the King and take up his throne.  Enroth soon fell unto my clutches and all paid homage to me, their new Lich King.  I crushed and diminished every rebellion and ruled for some years with utter asurety.

It didn't last long though.  A band of rebellious Enrothian Knights, led by the King's eldest daughter, Elizabeth, started questioning my authority.  It would be easy for me to quell their meager rebellion, If only my Necromancers were true to their King.  

A treacherous cult of Necromancers sided with the Queen just when the battle was dire and ensured my demise.  It seems I was way too cruel to my commanders for my own good.

I lost everything and was banished from the land.  Enroth is off limits, as the new Queen casted an abolishment spell on me.  

I can't return... for now.
map.hc9_main:0.header.description: Archon must reach Tarnum's Tomb within a month to win this scenario.
map.hc9_main:0.header.name: The Once and Future King
map.hc9_main:0.heroes.66.biography: A rebelous cult of Necromancers overthrew Archon, the Lich King of Enroth and Queen Elizabeth took over control of the throne.  That won't last for long though.  Archon is already plotting his revenge.
map.hc9_main:0.heroes.66.name: Archon
map.hc9_main:0.quest.31.17.1.completed:
You place the Cloak of the Undead King on the altar and start the ritual.  

A great and powerful wand is presented to you, a gift brought to you by the powers of darkness.  

You pick it up and cast the reanimation spell onto Tarnum's body.  It has begun!
map.hc9_main:0.quest.31.17.1.firstVisit:
After all your struggles, you eventually reach Tarnum's tomb.  In order to reanimate his undead body a great sacrifice has to be made.  

You need to weaken yourself and share your undead lifeforce with his.  You must surrender all of your power before the altar.

Do you accept?
map.hc9_main:0.quest.31.17.1.nextVisit: Without the Cloak of the Undead King, Tarnum's body will remain a corpse.
map.hc9_main:1.event.0.description:
You never realize how great life really is... till you die.

That wretched ex-king Archon used all of his powers to reanimate my corpse and return me back to life… as an undead corpse that is.  He is weakened by the process but still holds his pompous stature...  He dares to call me his "pet".

"The time will come my pet when we will rule all of Antagarich.  With your prowess and my dominative powers over the undead, the world will be MINE!"  He didn't even have the decency to try and say "ours".  He can have his moment... for now.
map.hc9_main:1.event.1.description:
The Lich King found it poetical to harvest our much needed undead forces from the bodies of my Barbarian tribes (ex-tribes anyway).  He was wondering if I would feel any remorse when I kill my own countrymen.  I didn't fail him though.  Wherever I went, carnage would ensue.

If someone would try and describe the undead with one word he would have to use "numbness".  I can't feel anything anymore... at least nothing decent, like mercy or guilt for all the destruction and the pillaging I bring unto my own people.  Indeed, there was a time, back when I was still alive, that my pride took over and I slaughtered mercilessly anyone I encountered.  

I seem more relentless now and the only power that motivates me is the lust for power itself.
map.hc9_main:1.event.2.description:
Harvesting isn't the only reason we pillage this region.  It seems that the Lich King's mind is drawn by a higher power that rests in this sorry part of the world.  He often speaks for a long forgotten power, the power of the God Wars that was buried beneath the sands of the Desolate Lands.

Through his readings, the Lich King confirmed the resting place of an Ancient temple, where an Ancient undead God was worshipped, centuries ago.  He bid me muster my Dread Knights and embark on a quest to find this forgotten shrine and reveal its secrets.
map.hc9_main:1.event.3.description:
My spies report that a great Death Knight of old named Lamentia, was imprisoned in a dark mansion somewhere in this area.  Imprisoned might be not the right word for it, since there are no guards really, just her own ghosts that haunt her and make her keep to her own.

I found out that she used to be a Barbarian herself when she was alive.  It would be nice to keep her as my concubine and let her warm my bed... if that's ever possible for an undead corpse that is.  She might prove herself to be a great asset to my army as well.
map.hc9_main:1.event.4.description:
The Lich King finally tracked the temple down.  It lies somewhere in the south.  It seems that the Barbarian tribes that live in these here hills are guarding it, although its secrets might be lost to them as well.  It would not surprise me if the Barbarians guarded it out of sheer stubbornness and have forgotten what it was about in the first place.  Their misplaced notion of honor amuses me.

Archon found an ancient tome that refers to the ancient Sand Gods and their Emissaries of War.  It seems there are four of them left in this world.  Two of them serve the Light and the other two were consumed by darkness.  The famous Anubites can be found somewhere in these lands.  
My master is assured that an Emissary of the great Anubis can be found in that temple.  If the guards can be defeated then the Anubite may be persuaded to join the ranks of his liberator.
map.hc9_main:1.event.5.description:
The Barbarians send me a message this morning:

"To the Undead Scum that calls itself Tarnum,

We don't know what your business is here, but we suggest you take it elsewhere.  And If you think that taking up the name of our Barbarian King Tarnum the Mad will frighten us then you're awfully misguided.

Leave now, in peace."

The Lich King laughed at me when I related the Barbarians' letter to him.  

"Don't worry my pet… They will not live long enough to recognize you.  They will soon be all part of my undead army."
map.hc9_main:1.event.6.description:
I am getting close now... Soon the power of Anubis will be sided with my own.  Thankfully, the Lich King is still weak and will never restore his former strength without the Cloak of the Undead King.

He still thinks he is in control though.  I can take advantage of that.  I will let him think he is my mighty King and act like the mindless brute that he thinks I am.  When the time is right I will overthrow him and seize control over his legions of the undead.  

I need him right now, to guide me through the powers of the great darkness but as soon as I grasp these powers, I won't be needing him at all.
map.hc9_main:1.event.7.description:
It seems that the reanimation worked partially.  Most part of my soul still lingers in the Hall of Judgment.  I asked one of the Liches why wasn't I fully reanimated.  It explained to me that when somebody is turned into an undead corpse he can never be whole again.  Only the lesser part of his soul is restored (the part responsible for all the atrocities I committed as the Barbarian King) and the greater part still rests in peace.

It matters not... It is true that my Barbarian self was capable of great deeds of honor and mercy but it was also allured by the bloodthirstiness and the wake of destruction.  As a newly animated Death Knight I won't need the good part of my soul anyway.  I am finally free to still my thirst for the blood of my enemies, deprived of the consequences of my actions.
map.hc9_main:1.header.description: Tarnum must reach the Temple of Anubis to win this scenario.  All Heroes will be limited to level 8, but Tarnum and Lamentia will transfer to the next scenario.  If Tarnum is defeated in battle all will be lost.
map.hc9_main:1.header.name: Genesis
map.hc9_main:1.heroes.150.biography: A few years after the fall of Bracaduun, a Knight named Rion Gryphonheart gave rise to a new kingdom known as Erathia. Tarnum was killed in battle by the young King. Tarnum's soul now resides in the Hall of Judgement, where three barbarian gods known as the Ancestors will judge him. In the meanwhile, the Lich King of Deyja uses Tarnum's reanimated corpse for his own twisted reasons.
map.hc9_main:1.heroes.150.name: Tarnum
map.hc9_main:1.heroes.68.biography: Lamentia used to be a Barbarian woman, but died during the independence war of her people, along with her four brothers in arms.  She's now turned into a Death Knight, but still the ghosts of the past haunt her and make her grief for her family's losses.
map.hc9_main:1.heroes.68.name: Lamentia
map.hc9_main:1.monster.4.19.0.message:
A group of Wights roams the plains near this forsaken mansion.  It would seem they were guarding it but in fact they just float about in the air, pointlessly.

You ask them what they do here...  There was no respond.

You enter the mansion and find out there is an undead woman there.  She used to be a great warrior princess of old.  You persuade her to join your army.
map.hc9_main:1.quest.3.10.0.completed:
You enter the Tower and find yourself surrounded by some ghosts from the past.  You seem to recognize them, but you don't remember their names.

One of them, offers you a hideous mask. You reluctantly take it.
map.hc9_main:1.quest.3.10.0.firstVisit: This mighty Tower used to be the Headquarters of an old and forsaken brotherhood of knights. Their Order was destroyed long ago... It seems that only ghosts roam the high battlements nowadays...
map.hc9_main:2.event.0.description:
This is the region where the Chaos Sanctuary is located.  I sent forth Lamentia to establish a base of operations for me.  This time I will be able to recruit some additional undead forces rather than rely to my trusted Dread Knights.  Still, I will need their prowess in order to claim victory.

This region used to be Barbarian territory but now belongs to the new upstart nation of Erathia.  There still is a great harbor in the South though, where some brigands and pirates lay sway.  My scouts report that there is a commander that calls himself the Pirate King of the Dalkha.  His name is Salah and used to be a Barbarian Warchief of mine, when I was alive and still King of these lands.  

It matters not.  If he stands in my way, he will end up as one of my undead minions.
map.hc9_main:2.event.1.description:
The Anubis Warrior that has followed us here presented to me a map of the waters that I have to cross to reach the Chaos Sanctuary.  The Erathians organized their defenses well.  

They say that there are a lot of Barbarian Warchiefs that bent the knee and now swear fealty to this new nation.  The once proud people of old are brought now low and currently serve as glorified knights in King Rion's guard. 

I enjoy slaughtering these traitorous Erathian Knights.  They used to be MY subjects. Now they'll join the ranks of my undead minions and serve me once again.
map.hc9_main:2.event.2.description:
The so called Pirate King, Salah, sent me a letter this morning:

Listen here Death Knight,

These lands and the high seas that surround them are my domain!  They are mine to plunder, pillage and loot so go back to the rat infested home of yours and rot there instead.

Salah, King of Pirates (and their Wenches!) 
 
There is grog spilled all over the piece of paper.  I like this puny little pirate.  Once I reanimate his dead corpse I will keep him around as my jester.  I find his lack of perspective very amusing.
map.hc9_main:2.event.3.description:
My scouts report that there are a few keymaster tents that need to be visited before I can even try to reach the Chaos Sanctuary.  The Anubis warrior teleported to all three of them and found out that they need to be visited in the correct order to gain passage to the temple.  I must hire some more scouts from the taverns that lay in abundance in these pirate infested lands, in order to find them quickly.

I need to pay attention to Salah's movements as well.  He may be a drunken Pirate lord but he knows the sea better than me and may find the temple before me (even by accident).  I can't allow this.
map.hc9_main:2.event.4.description:
My spies report that there is a whirlpool located just out the southern coast.  It may lead to the resting place of the Chaos Sanctuary.  Some old sailors tell tales of brave men that survived the whirlpool and found a passage to tides beyond, and a place of fiery waters, riddled with flame waves and crimson tides.  

This sounds like a place where the lost temple might be.
map.hc9_main:2.event.5.description:
These Erathians are tougher than I thought.  Not only do they use iron forged steel and heavy armory (even for their horses) but they also use the combined forces of the mighty griffins and the forces of Heaven as well.

Still, they are no match for my undead army.  The darkness will prevail and my powers will grow beyond proportion soon enough.  The bloodthirstiness of my Barbarian body is now merged with the consuming powers of the undead.  I will soon be invincible.
map.hc9_main:2.event.6.description:
The Lich King summoned me to his tent this morning:

-Aahh my pet... Come in, come in... You have served me well my pet, and so I thought a little treat was in order.

Pinned down to the flour was a pack of wretched Erathian prisoners (farmers no doubt) which were probably tortured and mutilated for hours after hours.  I suppose the Lich King expected me to kill them and reanimate their corpses.

-What's the matter my pet?  Did Tarnum the great Warchief lose his nerve? - He started a sinister chuckle.

This was obviously a power game and I can't be seen as a weakling before this lowlife puppet king.

-I will not kill them my lord.  I will keep them alive and enslave them.  Teach them that there are fates worse than death!

I left the tent dragging the slaves with me.  Eventually, I guess this is what I became after all.  A ruthless Death Knight, deprived of all that's good and pure.
map.hc9_main:2.guards.15.9.1.message: Near one of the Shipwrecks you notice a floating Pandora's Box.  There's no telling what horrors (or treasures) can be found within.
map.hc9_main:2.header.description: Tarnum must reach the Chaos Sanctuary to win this scenario.  If the Pirate Lord Salah reaches it before Tarnum does then all is lost.  All Heroes will be limited to level 14, but Tarnum and Lamentia will transfer to the next scenario.
map.hc9_main:2.header.name: The Chaos Within
map.hc9_main:2.heroes.188.biography: Salah deems himself as the supreme Pirate King. Pirates and Wenches alike pledge their loyalty to him, although it is said that most of them are allured by the gold he offers them rather than his leadership skills.
map.hc9_main:2.heroes.188.name: Salah
map.hc9_main:2.quest.15.31.0.firstVisit:
This outpost seems to belong to the Pirate King.

There's nothing of interest here, except maybe a few empty bottles of Grog.
map.hc9_main:2.quest.7.14.0.completed: When you offered the undead soldiers the full sum of Gold, they presented you their chains, as a token of submission to your will.
map.hc9_main:2.quest.7.14.0.firstVisit:
This great Watch Tower once belonged to King Rion Gryphonheart of Erathia. However, after the Barbarians attacked, it seems that the King has abandoned his claims over this land. The garrison was abandoned to meet its damnation. 100 Halberdiers were guarding this tower and were surely overwhelmed by the Barbarian raiding forces sooner rather than later... Most of them are turned into undead soldiers now. 

You bargain with them and they offer their services to you (as mercenaries) for 10000 gold. In better days this price would be most unacceptable indeed, but you'll need all the help you can get. They'll be waiting for you here.
map.hc9_main:3.event.0.description:
The combined tainted blessings of Anubis and Sekhmet are now on our disposal.  Archon is now fully revived.  Their powers have fully restored his physical form and he is now more potent than ever.  Still, there's a lot left to do to regain his throne.

First things first. We need to repay the gods for their blessings.  Unholy deities need sacrifices to be appealed, lest we want their wrath unleashed upon us.  They demand that we repay in blood for their aid.

To be exact, the power gods demand the blood of their enemies, the Sun Gods.  They want their temples brought low, and the temple guardians slaughtered and offered as sacrificial victims to them.  This is why the Lich King dragged us to this forsaken place.
map.hc9_main:3.event.1.description:
There are a few Barbarian tribes that guard the entrance to the Desolate Lands.  They must be crushed before we would venture to this endless wasteland.  Their Nomadic allies that guard the Sun Gods' temples reside in a place called Sandstorm's Reach, a great desert with nothing of consequence in it.

My undead minions cannot bear sunlight with ease.  If I cross the portal that merges these two lands I will have to procure a great striking force.  That's another reason to defeat the Barbarian tribes first and reanimate as much as their corpses as possible.  The sunlight will take its toll once we reach the desert and so it is imperative that I have enough skeletons to spare.
map.hc9_main:3.event.2.description:
I consulted my shamans and witch doctors on how I am to pass the desert without having my troops incinerated by this blasted sunlight.  They won't last a day in these deserts.  I cannot risk my own demise in that way as well.  Now that I am an undead corpse, I can't stand the sun for long.

The shamans reached a verdict soon enough.  I need to devise a mobile Cover of Darkness, to scorch the sky and block out the sun.  I asked the Sekhmet Priestess for a thread of her dark cloak.  The magical powers that lay in her vestments might do the trick.  I know that my shamans will find a way.  I warned them that if they don't find a way, I'll personally bash their heads open.  This will keep them properly motivated.
map.hc9_main:3.event.3.description:
The Anubis Warrior and the Sekhmet Priestess were waiting for me in my tent this evening.  They never talk.  They communicate telepathically.  It does fill the listener with dread this way (even if it is an undead Warlord as me).

They were wondering what I am doing here, under the command of this pompous Lich.  They realize the magnitude of my prowess in both battle and malice.  They suggested that I was meant to rule instead of that sorry sort of a Lich King.  In the end they presented me with a parchment of a scroll.

I tried reading the scroll but the hieroglyphics in it were undecipherable.  By the time I turned to them for help they were gone.  They never came back ever since.
map.hc9_main:3.event.4.description:
The Lich King summoned me to his tent this morning:

-What do you think you're doing my pet?  You chased the God Emissaries away!  Do you defy my authority, you worthless worm?

I immidiately knew that this needed to be handled with care.  The Lich King has regained much of his former strength and might prove to be a formidable opponent.  I tried to be diplomatic.

-No my lord, I wouldn't dream of it.  I have always served you, my lord.  The Emissaries left on their own accord.

The Lich King seemed to believe me.  It was no lie after all.  I just left the part where they presented me with that ancient scroll.

-All right, all right my pet.  I believe you.  Even you wouldn't be stupid enough to lie to me, isn't that right my pet?   

-Yes my lord.  Certainly too dumb to lie.

His arrogance is his weakness and will soon be his downfall.  I can control him, as long as I reassure his fragile ego.
map.hc9_main:3.event.5.description:
I've been trying to decipher the ancient scroll the Emissaries gave me.  There are at least three dozen symbols in it.  I know that every three or four symbols can be deciphered into one single letter from the alphabet used in the common tongue.

I need to find a way to learn its secrets, but how?  I can't ask anyone for help, as it might raise suspicion.  And I am not powerful enough to challenge the Lich King to a game of thrones.  He'll have to remain the Lich King.  For now...
map.hc9_main:3.event.6.description:
I woke up this morning, only to find Lamentia reading the scroll!  I've been summoning her to my tent at night for quite a while now, and allowed her to be my personal concubine, but I never thought she'd have the nerve to go through my stuff!

I raised my Dread Sword in an attempt to slice her in half but she avoided the blow.  She used to be a Barbarian after all, and still knows her way around a fight.  That's why I liked her in the first place.

-Wait Tarnum!  I am not trying to undermine you.  I am trying to help you.

I stayed my wrath for a little while, to see what she'd have to say for herself.  She continued:

-Maybe it is time I revealed myself...

I startled.  Who is she?  What does she mean by that?  Do we know each other?

-You don't recognize me.  It is surely understandable.  Time has decayed my undead body even more than your own, and my features might be severely damaged.

I grew impatient with this guessing game.  -Who are you?-  I shouted, lifting my sword once again.

-Yalla!
map.hc9_main:3.event.7.description:
Over the past few days Yalla (now Lamentia) told me everything.  She said she lost her life alongside four fellow Barbarians who served my cause (when I was still a mere Barbarian rebel).  Darkness took her and she strayed out of thought and time.  She was reanimated into a Death knight, until vengeance could be found to redeem her.

She said that she scouted the desolate lands by herself when I was not paying much attention to her movements.  She said she found some lost temples in the withering sands, and within their tombs, some hieroglyphics could be found, same as the scroll's hieroglyphics.  Within these tombs could be the key to decipher them.

She pledged her loyalty to me and proclaimed that she would follow me to whatever end.  She would have the Emissaries' request fulfilled and see me the new King of this land, a new undead King.  As soon as we find these temples and decipher the scroll, this future can be ours!
map.hc9_main:3.header.description: Tarnum must defeat all enemies to win this scenario.  All Heroes will be limited to level 20, but Tarnum and Lamentia will transfer to the next scenario.  If Tarnum is defeated in battle all will be lost.
map.hc9_main:3.header.name: Gods of War
map.hc9_main:3.quest.9.34.0.completed: The shaman quietly looks at you and sneers...  He offers you a small voodoo doll, in exchange for your abscence.  You accept his offer.
map.hc9_main:3.quest.9.34.0.firstVisit: Inside the hut, lives a lonely shaman.  You enter his home.
map.hc9_main:4.event.0.description:
I established a base and bid Lamentia to follow me here.  The map drove us deep within the now ruined empire of Bracaduun.  Since their defeat, the Wizards started rebuilding and named this land Bracada.  They always lacked imagination as far as names would go.  

There is also a sizeable force of Erathian military in the region.  They might prove to be a problem as my spies report; their leaders are, unknowingly, guarding the entrance to this ancient Necropolis.  I'll have to defeat them as well, in order to gain access to the city.  I need to be quick about it too, before one of them dares to venture near the Necropolis and find out (even by accident) that there is a great power there.
map.hc9_main:4.event.1.description:
I sent out scouts to scour the area for clues that might help me gain access to the city.  I need to find a way to open the passageway to the city's outer walls.  My spies report that I need to find a few teleporters:  Two white as snow and one tan colored.  My enemies may find them first so I need to act quickly.

I need to harvest a lot of skeletons and zombies to prepare a formidable striking force.  The snows of Bracada form a much better harvesting ground than the desert lands that were filled with holy sunlight.  Here the night is dark and long, and the winter's chill procures lots of fresh corpses to reanimate.  It seems that the weather of the world supports my quest.
map.hc9_main:4.event.2.description:
The Lich King summoned me to my tent this morning:

-Aaahh… my pet.  Come in, come in…  Enjoying the weather much?

This wretched scum is now all politeness.  He deems himself flattered by the idea that I embarked on this quest to bestow more power onto him.  He still calls me his pet though, a way to reassure himself on who is in command.  Poor wretch!

-Yes milord.  Death sure takes its toll in these snow infested lands, and when it does we will be right there to collect!

-Fine, fine my pet…  I am very proud of you.  As soon as the secrets of Blackwater are revealed to me and I gain more strength than ever, we will embark for Enroth.  Nothing will stop us then!

Nothing but me.  I have my own plans for the time this ancient city is conquered.  The Lich King continued.

-But first, we need to retrieve something of mine.  A thing that will ensure my rise to power.

-What is it sire?

-Oh, you'll see my pet…  Oh yes, you will see!
map.hc9_main:4.event.3.description:
Our last meeting with the Lich King has baffled me.  Is there something I missed?  Does the Lich King have some secret plans that weren't entrusted even to me?

I need to hurry up and find the Necropolis.  Once I claim its secrets I will be powerful enough to challenge the Lich King's authority and take over his armies' command.  When that happens, I will surely find a way to "persuade" him to tell me his secret plans.
map.hc9_main:4.event.4.description:
My spies have returned with some news.  They report that there are a more than a few bands of Bracadian troops that guard these lands.  It seems that they have established bases in strategic places across the land.  The Erathian Castles support their quest.

It seems that this land is full of novelties... Diamond Dragons have been sighted to the skies...  Lords of Thunder may be seen here as well.  I need to prepare my army well before I dare face them in battle.

It will be extremely difficult to reach these teleporters.  My spies report that the teleporters lead to two islands, where the Erathians hold sway.  I need to strike them hard and swift.  If they decide to capture the town before me, then all will be lost.  They may presume to harvest the power of the Necropolis themselves, if I am too late.  Let's hope that doesn't happen.
map.hc9_main:4.event.5.description:
I am getting close now.  Soon the town will be mine and I will be at last master of my own fate.  Once I overthrow this puppet-King, I will command the legions of the undead and make them do my own biding. 

And then what?  I was pondering on what my next move should be.  I could just continue to conquer land after land, reanimate corpse after corpse, until the end of time.  Will this be enough?

I don't think so…  Eternity can be a drag and I will regret it forever if I don't take this opportunity and claim that which a Barbarian (and even more a Death Knight) would hold most dear in his whole existence:

Revenge!
map.hc9_main:4.event.6.description:
Deep within a vault, buried inside a temple of Anubis, there lay a plaque of hieroglyphics, a plaque that contained the secret of the decipherment of the ancient scroll the Emissaries gave me.  I was finally able to read the scroll and find out that a single name was written:  Blackwater.  Upon reading the name out loud, a map was magically drawn in the back of the scroll.  It showed the exact location of what appeared to be an Ancient Necropolis.

The city's location is a mystery.  The map inticates that in order to reach it, one must make a leap of faith through the void, to travel to the very edge of the world.

It seems that an ancient power resided within the ruins of that city, a power that is ripe for the taking, for whoever was bold enough to venture there.  I needed to persuade the Lich King that it was HE that was destined to harness it.  It took a lot of arguing but eventually I convinced him to allow me to search for this Necropolis and claim this power for him - or so he thought.
map.hc9_main:4.event.7.description:
The enemy knows why I am here. 

My spies report that all the shipyards and docks in the islands were demolished.  However, my enemy still moves around...

Wizards... They probably think they have outsmarted me.  There are other ways to cross the sea.  I am no mindless Barbarian anymore.  The powers of Darkness have granted me the gift of spellcasting.

There are more than a few spells that might work... I could summon a boat from the Underworld, a cursed ship to take me to the shores of the Ancient Necropolis.  Some of my shamans even suggest I try walking on water as well! 

Where there's a will, there is a way.
map.hc9_main:4.header.description: Tarnum must capture the Necropolis town of Blackwater before his enemies do to win this scenario. Heroes will be limited to level 24, but Tarnum and Lamentia will transfer to the next scenario. If Tarnum is defeated in battle all will be lost.
map.hc9_main:4.header.name: Damnation
map.hc9_main:4.quest.9.24.1.completed:
The shaman quietly looks at you and sneers...  Again!

-So...  We meet again.  I see that you are Hideous, wrought Despair and practiced Voodoo.  Is it too late for you?  Time will tell I guess.  

You do not follow his meaning at all.  He is starting to get on your nerves.  Before you reach for your sword, the shaman vanishes...  In his place, a small charm emerges.  You decide to keep it.
map.hc9_main:4.quest.9.24.1.firstVisit: You're surprised to see that inside the hut, lives the same shaman that gave you his Voodoo Doll.  You enter his home.
map.hc9_main:4.town.33.27.0.name: Blackwater
map.hc9_main:5.event.0.description:
When I found the ancient city of Blackwater, I felt its power surging through my body.  I felt wiser, quicker and stronger.  I claimed these powers for my own and proclaimed myself master of Blackwater.

The Lich King was not pleased of course.  He ordered his legions to attack the Castle walls and bring him my head.  Alas, my power was too great for his pathetic minions.  I single handedly defeated his hordes of Skeletons and Walking Dead and found myself amidst his encampment. 
I barged into his tent, grasped him by his throat and put him in a cage.  His minions soon perceived that the power play was over and I was the winner.  They all bowed to my own will.  I would soon be crowned their King!

However, that didn't happen.  The undead were mine to command true, but that was it.  I wasn't their King and I could see it into their empty eye sockets.  They followed me to be sure, but out of fear and not loyalty.
map.hc9_main:5.event.1.description:
I visited Archon in his prison cell and asked the former Lich King why this came to be; why wasn't I crowned the undead King? All I got was a sinister chuckle.  He knew… he knew the reason.  But he wouldn't tell me.  Not willingly anyway.

He underestimated my new appointed powers for one more time.  I conjured up a truth spell and cast it upon him.  He would now tell me anything I needed to know.

He told me that his authority resided on his Cloak, the enchanted Cloak of the Undead King!  I thought it was destroyed when he reanimated my corpse.  It didn't.  It merely broke into the three distinct artifacts that form this relic.  All I need to do is to reclaim these artifacts.  This was his own plan all along.  He wouldn't leave Antagarich without theses artifacts.  

I need to find them and claim them for myself.
map.hc9_main:5.event.2.description:
But what about my needs?  When I first entered Blackwater I had one goal, and one goal only.  Revenge!  Revenge on this puny Erathian King, Rion Gryphonheart, the man that dared to kill me and claim my lands for his!

These were my plans all along after all.  The only reason I sided with Archon was for the promise of death that he gave me.  Death to all the living, thus to my Nemesis as well.  Now that the Lich King has been overthrown it is up to me to fulfill his destiny.  But what should I do first?  Attack and destroy Erathia, or Search for the Cloak?
map.hc9_main:5.event.3.description:
After giving it much thought, I decided to pursue both my goals at the same time.  I travelled far and soon found myself near the borders of Erathia and Bracada.  I decided to attack Erathia to this weak spot and establish a small base of operations.  Once this base is established, I will send Lamentia (my only general that I can truly trust) and bid her keep it for me, till I find the Cloak's pieces.

Lamentia agreed and so we started building up a Necropolis in the snow.  The Wizards were not happy that we treaded their lands of course.  They started building up their own armies and prepared their attack.  The Erathian Castle that protects the borders has been also warned of our movements. 

I don't need to win all of my enemies though.  Once I crush the defenses of these Wizard-scums, all I need to do is conquer the Erathian Castle town.  Once I accomplish this goal, I will fortify the area and leave Lamentia in charge, while I seek the artifacts.
map.hc9_main:5.event.4.description:
My spies report that the Castle's defenses are well organized.  They even report of a grail structure, that not only fills the defenders' hearts with courage, it also provides with additional growth in troops.

I need to make sure I have enough troops to break the lines of defense that hold this town intact.  I need to pay attention to the Wizards' movements as well, as they might prove to be a formidable opponent (should I underestimate them).
map.hc9_main:5.event.5.description:
A letter came this morning.  It was pinned in the back of a walking dead.  The enemy cut off his arms and sent it astray so that I may find it.

To the Death knight that roams these lands,

Disband your forces and leave.  You're no match for our combined forces.  Bracada and Erathia are allies in this.  We will crush you and feed your remains to the dogs!

Sir Mullich, defender of Erathia.

The little fool.  He thinks that his grail structure can match the infinite powers that I now posses, thanks to the dark gods' guidance.  When you have powerful allies like this, no force can hinder your will.  Even Sir Mullich's Angels and Archangels will bow or die before the onslaught I bring on their doorstep!
map.hc9_main:5.event.6.description:
Soon enough I will control this area and I will be able to embark on my side quest, on finding the great artifacts that will make me King of the Undead.  I dispatched some scouts and ordered them to visit all the remote places of this land and find information about the artifacts.
Days passed and none returned.  They probably were destroyed by the Wizards that guard the snowy paths.  I realize now that I have to search for them myself.  

The powers bestowed upon me by the gods and the Ancient Necropolis made me more perceptive and offered me the ability of second vision.  I sense the artifacts are near.  I will try and search for them as soon as I finished the Erathian invasion.
map.hc9_main:5.header.description: Capture the Castle town to win this scenario. Heroes will be limited to level 28, but Tarnum and Lamentia will transfer to the next scenario.  If Tarnum is defeated in battle all will be lost.
map.hc9_main:5.header.name: Change of Plans
map.hc9_main:5.monster.13.13.0.message:
Just when you were about to face the Titans, that wretched shaman appears one last time.  He raises his wand and takes your mask, chains and charms from your body.

He magically entwines them into something new, a powerful artifact.  He places this artifact unto the hands of the Titans' leader.  It will be hard to reclaim it, but you feel that it is worth the try.
map.hc9_main:6.event.0.description:
As soon as the land was secured, I sent Lamentia to organize the defense of the captured stronghold of men, near the Erathian borders.  She will lead the armies recruited in the Castle.  There is a twisted poetic justice in all this, having a Death Knight rule the Knights that caused her death in the first place.  She won't like it (although so will the Erathians as well).

As for me, I established a base of operations of my own.  I fortified myself in a Necropolis, located somewhat northeast of the Erathian borders.  I placed a Tower Guard to protect the entrance to the high peeks that protect my town.  The enemy will find it hard to gain access to the Necropolis.  It won't be impossible though, so I must be extra careful.

I sent out my scouts and finally had some vital information about my enemy's moves.  When the Erathians fled their homeland, the Wizards of Bracada regrouped and rallied their own forces, surrounding my keep.  This might have been bad news, but instead they are great!  It has been pointed out to me that three of these Wizards wear the artifacts I so much crave. 

Upon their defeat, my coronation will soon follow!
map.hc9_main:6.event.1.description:
Death will come to my enemies from both fronts.  Lamentia is mustering an army of Erathian renegades and is fortifying herself in the East, while my own undead forces will strike from the North.  The Wizards won't stand a change!

News of our great exploits has spread and the shadow of death has scorched the land.  It seems that the locals fear me a great deal now, so much as to give me a nickname:

King of Pain.

I like it.  I think I will keep it as my title when the coronation begins.  All I have to do is to gather the three artifacts that form the Cloak of the Undead King.
map.hc9_main:6.event.2.description:
Since I've never seen the artifacts that I am after, I dispatched some spies to inform me of what they look like.

The first one is an Amulet, an amulet shaped like a coffin.  My spy told me that its bearer is Halon the Wizard.  He told me that he seems willing to defend it with his life and that he will never allow it to leave his neck.  I will cut his pretty little neck and remove it with my bare hands!

The second artifact is a Vampire's Cowl and rests upon the shoulders of Astral.  He is said to be an expert in Hypnotize.  I will put out his eyes and see if that's still the case then.

As for the third artifact... it is merely a pair of Boots worn by the Wizard Serena.  I will cut off her legs and see if she'll still need boots in her life!

Once assembled, the three artifacts magically transform into one, the Cloak of the Undead King.  It will soon be mine!
map.hc9_main:6.event.3.description:
A scout reported some disturbing news this morning.

It seems that these Wizard-scums have formed a plan to counter attack, and it seems rather likely to work too.

There is a young Wizard's apprentice named Sandor.  He currently resides in a Storm Temple in the South.  It seems that this Sandor has been studying the arts of Necromancy!  Such studies are generally banned in the lands of men and this is why this Wizard is held captive in the mountain tops.

The troubling news is that the Wizards have come up with an idea.  If the battle goes ill and my forces will prevail, they will entrust their artifacts to this upstart Wizard and crown him the Undead King.  It seems that they prefer to give such power to one of their own, rather than risk me obtaining it.

This does not bow well.  If this Wizard is granted all this power then he may be even proven stronger than me.  All will be for nothing and the crown will fall into the lap of this witless worm.  I cannot allow this!
map.hc9_main:6.event.4.description:
What am I going to do?  I need to act quickly.  Strike my enemies now, before they grow strong beyond proportion.  For the power bestowed by the Cloak of the Undead King is too vast for any opposition.

I sent word to Lamentia to hasten her preparations.  She can't keep in the defensive anymore.  She needs to go forth and attack our enemies before they grow too strong!  I will make the same preparations in my territory.
map.hc9_main:6.event.5.description:
A letter arrived for me this morning:

Death knight,

Do not force us to bestow this great power that you seek to one of our own.  Such power needs to remain hidden and not be unleashed upon this world.  Do this, and your wretched existence will be spared.  We will not pursuit you.  You'll be free to flee these lands.  You have our word.

The Bracadian Wizards

Last time a Wizard gave me his word, all of my Barbarian troops were slaughtered!  I cannot trust these enchanters with anything.  My only way to deal with them is to destroy them altogether.  I am now resolved.  They must all die!
map.hc9_main:6.event.6.description:
Things are going better than expected.  I don't know if the Wizards assembled the artifacts for themselves but either way I will be ready.  I have managed to gain control of a sizeable force and will continue to push till I reach the Erathian borders (with the Undead Cloak of course).

When I am done here I will finally be ready to fulfill my darkest desire:  To challenge King Rion Gryphonheart himself!  I will be ready for him now and I won't fail this time.  This time I will not be just a meager Barbarian Warchief.  I will be King of the Undead, the incarnation of Death itself!  There will be no power in the world that can stop me then.

And I'll finally have my vengeance!
map.hc9_main:6.event.7.description:
A lowly figure crept in my tent this morning.  How did she manage to escape my guards?  I raised my hand to strike her down, but she lowered it with a small gesture.  There is great power in this woman I could tell.  She seemed harmless though and so I calmly asked her what she was after.

She starred at me and opened her mouth.  Her voice was deep and outwardly, as if it came from beyond. She said:

"And the fell King will meet the King of Light in battle once more!  But this time, the death blow will be stricken by both of them!  For, neither can live while the other survives!"

A prophecy!  That's what this woman is, a prophet!

Before I could respond or actually do anything, she vanished before my eyes in a sparkling smoke of pure Light.  She was gone.
map.hc9_main:6.header.description: Tarnum must assemble the Cloak of the Undead King and reach the Castle town to win this scenario. Heroes will be limited to level 32 but Tarnum will transfer to the next scenario. If Tarnum falls in battle all will be lost.
map.hc9_main:6.header.name: Undead King
map.hc9_main:6.heroes.45.biography: Sandor is a young Wizard's apprentice that currently resides in a Cloud Temple.  His studying over the arts of Necromancy are generally banned in the lands of men and this is why this Wizard is held captive in the mountain tops.
map.hc9_main:6.heroes.45.name: Sandor
map.hc9_main:7.event.0.description:
It has come to this...  The greatest battle of our time.

Both Erathian and Barbarian forces have rallied forth to meet my own forces of the undead.  They managed to break the lines of my bannermen and destroy most of my striking force.  They even destroyed and burned down Lamentia's body!  She is gone for good now...

It matters not...  The world of men shall fall...  I still stand, and with the aid of my enchanted Cloak of the Undead King I will detsroy them!  Erathia will bleed and diminish!

I rejoice in the thought that I will meet that wretched scum, King Rion Gryphonheart in battle, one last time.  However, the prophecy still rings in my ears:

"And the fell King will meet the King of Light in battle once more!  But this time, the death blow will be stricken by both of them!  For, neither can live while the other survives!"

It seems that King Gryphonheart is meant to defeat me once more.  This time however, vengeance will be brought upon him.  I will gladly trade all of my powers, all of my hard conquered lands, even my own undead life, just to see him draw his last breath!

And so I shall...  It ends...  Here and now!
map.hc9_main:7.header.description: Tarnum must defeat all enemies to win this scenario.  If Tarnum is defeated in battle all will be lost.
map.hc9_main:7.header.name: The Glory of War
map.hc9_main:7.heroes.152.name: Rion
